selection.rationale: The frozen workload is one pipeline() call on (256, 4096) FP32 inputs, timed as CUDA-synced wall latency, on a single device with no communication (resources.json: communication not_applicable). Coverage is complete (15/15 CUDA kernels associated with the run phase, no unassociated or backward kernels), so the observed region is the entire cost. The pipeline executes 15 sequential small kernels (13 pipeline-phase groups: mul x3, add x3, sub x2, sin, cos, sigmoid, pow, rsqrt, mean x2), each only ~1-4 us diagnostic CUDA time on a 4 MB tensor. Nested diagnostic CUDA time is 53.054 us while the clean measured baseline latency is 0.1738 ms, so roughly two thirds of the project metric is kernel-launch/dispatch overhead and inter-kernel gaps rather than GPU compute; reducing the number of launched kernels directly moves the requested metric. The chain is also memory-bound and redundant: the elementwise sequence performs ~15 full-tensor read/write passes (~60+ MB of traffic for 4 MB tensors), and 'wave - mean' is computed twice (sub group ae93b2b2bf41a25fd1e7, invocations=2; calls.json count=2) — once for variance and once for normalized. All elementwise groups plus the two mean reductions form one contiguous, coherently editable region (the pipeline body in the adapter/source), and the fusion edits are interdependent (reusing the centered tensor and fusing the affine/trig epilogue only pay off as one rewrite), so they are proposed as a single region candidate rather than per-group edits. The project.invoke call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 is additionally affected because its child execution and measured duration change, though it is not itself edited. The profiler record_function enter/exit calls (a60da373fdd5a4383277bf4e, ca1f233e0c891270f758ff58) are discovery instrumentation, not project source, and are unchanged by the proposal. No reordering across unknown dependencies is involved: the region is pure, single-stream, stateless functional code with data edges internal to the region, and semantics (FP32, TF32 off, exact pipeline math, all 1048576 outputs) are preserved.
selection.hypothesis: Rewriting the pipeline body as a fused implementation — computing centered = wave - mean once, fusing the affine -> sin+cos elementwise chain, and fusing the normalize/gating epilogue around the two dim=-1 mean reductions (e.g., via torch.compile/Inductor-generated kernels or an equivalent hand-fused formulation) — reduces kernel launches from 15 to roughly 4-5 and full-tensor memory passes from ~15 to ~5, eliminating one redundant 4 MB sub pass and most per-launch overhead. This is expected to lower CUDA-synced wall latency from the 0.1738 ms baseline toward ~0.08-0.12 ms while keeping every FP32 output element within atol=rtol=1e-5 (same math, same reduction dimension, TF32 disabled). This is a hypothesis to be tested by the framework's paired measurement and observe()-based correctness check, not an accepted benefit; the improvement threshold is 0.0 so any verified latency reduction with intact outputs qualifies.

proposal.rationale: Region rewrite of the entire pipeline body through the project.invoke call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (adapter.run), matching the selected region scope. Observed facts from the supplied artifacts: the frozen workload is exactly one pipeline() call on (256, 4096) FP32 CUDA tensors; the clean baseline latency is 0.173762 ms (inputs/project.json original_baseline) while nested diagnostic CUDA time for the same run phase is 53.054 us across 15 kernels (inputs/target-resources.json, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0), so roughly two thirds of the measured latency is per-kernel launch/dispatch overhead and inter-kernel gaps rather than GPU math. The chain performs 15 kernel launches over 4 MB tensors (three muls, three adds, two subs, sin, cos, sigmoid, pow, rsqrt, two mean reductions; the mean.dim and sub.Tensor sites are each invoked twice per run), i.e. ~15 full-tensor memory passes, and 'wave - mean' is computed twice. Hypothesis (subject to the framework's paired measurement, not an accepted benefit): computing the whole body in ONE fused Triton kernel - one program per row that loads x/scale/bias, computes the affine, forms sin+cos, block-reduces the row mean, forms the centered row once, block-reduces the variance, and applies rsqrt(variance + 1e-5) plus the sigmoid-gate epilogue in registers - reduces launches from 15 to 1 and full-tensor passes to ~3 (read x, write output; scale/bias are 16 KB broadcast reads), which should move CUDA-synced wall latency well below the baseline while keeping every FP32 output element within the frozen atol=rtol=1e-5. The kernel uses the same libdevice sin/cos/sigmoid primitives and FP32 arithmetic as the ATen kernels; only reduction order differs (bounded by a few ULPs, see quality_risks). Robustness: the Triton path is gated at build time by a one-shot equivalence check against the verbatim reference math (boolean outcome only, nothing cached; the kernel still executes on every invocation); if Triton or the gate is unavailable, the candidate degrades to a CUDA-graph replay of the verbatim eager op sequence (bit-identical math to the parent, single replay launch instead of 15 dispatches), and failing that to a reduced-launch eager sequence (addcmul, fused var_mean, silu). Every replacement checks the observed signature properties per call (shape, dtype, device, contiguity, no-grad; the graph path additionally requires the exact captured input tensors) and otherwise falls back to the parent adapter.run, preserving the run/observe ABI and the 'output' result structure. eliminated_calls lists the 13 inner aten call sites: their only consumer is the pipeline body itself, which this replacement reproduces end-to-end; the sole external consumer (result['output'] -> observe()/metrics()) receives a freshly computed, correctly shaped FP32 tensor each invocation, so downstream behavior stays valid and the framework can recapture the plan. inputs/previous-feedback.txt does not exist, so there is no prior attempt feedback to incorporate.

setup_work.one_time_build_cost: Triton JIT compilation of exactly one kernel specialization (rows=256, WIDTH=4096, fp32, num_warps from parameter_space) plus one probe launch and one eager reference computation for the equivalence gate; results are discarded and nothing fixture-dependent is cached (typically a few seconds, CPU-bound). Fallback path only: side-stream warmup and CUDA-graph capture of the verbatim 15-op sequence.
setup_work.persistent_gpu_memory: Triton path: no persistent allocations; steady state allocates one fresh (256, 4096) FP32 output (~4.2 MB) per invocation, below the baseline's ~29.4 MB peak allocated intermediates. Graph fallback path: a graph-private pool holding the static intermediates plus the static output (~29 MB), plus a ~4.2 MB clone per invocation.
setup_work.model_transformations: None. The project has no nn.Module roots, no parameters, and no caches; the prepared input tensors are read-only and untouched.

quality_risks: Reduction-order deltas: the fused kernel's per-thread partial sums and block tree differ from ATen's mean/pow/mean two-pass reduction order, shifting mean/variance by a few ULPs (estimated ~1e-6 absolute on the final output), about 10x inside the frozen atol=rtol=1e-5.

FMA contraction: Triton/LLVM may contract x*scale + bias into a single-rounding FMA while the reference rounds the product first (<= 1 ULP of affine, <= ~4e-7 propagated through sin/cos), still well inside tolerance.

tl.sigmoid/tl.exp may lower to an exp2-based fast exponential (~2 ulp relative error), contributing at most a few 1e-6 absolute error at large |normalized|; margins remain >2x against the frozen thresholds.

Mitigation: a build-time allclose gate at atol=rtol=5e-6 (2x tighter than the frozen thresholds) runs the fused kernel and the verbatim reference math once on the prepared inputs; failure demotes the candidate to the bit-identical CUDA-graph path. The kernel is deterministic (no atomics, fixed reduction tree, same binary), so the gate outcome predicts the framework's check on the same device.

Graph fallback: replay writes a static buffer; each invocation returns static_out.clone(), preserving the reference's fresh-output alias semantics, and the path is identity-guarded to the exact captured input tensors with parent fallback otherwise.

Any signature mismatch (shape/stride/dtype/device/requires_grad) or runtime error on any path falls back to the parent adapter.run for that invocation, so external outputs and result structure are always preserved.
No autograd or state interactions: the workload is stateless inference on requires_grad=False inputs (project invariant), and no in-place rewrites touch parent-owned storage.

external_invariants: Workload is exactly one pipeline() invocation on the fixed inputs (rows=256, width=4096, seed=91273); the work amount must not change.
All computation in FP32 with torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False, matching the source policy.

Input construction uses a single torch.Generator on the bound device seeded with the workload seed, drawing x = randn(rows, width), scale = randn(width)*0.1+1, bias = randn(width)*0.05 in that order, so tensors are bit-identical to the source's.

pipeline semantics preserved exactly: affine = x*scale+bias; wave = sin(affine)+cos(affine); mean/variance over dim=-1 with keepdim; normalized = (wave-mean)*rsqrt(variance+1e-5); output = normalized*sigmoid(normalized).
Every output element (256*4096 = 1048576 FP32 values) is part of correctness and must be returned by observe() as a detached tensor.
Timing boundaries are CUDA-synchronized wall time surrounding run(), matching the source's perf_counter_ns + synchronize pattern; no internal profiler or partial-phase timing is substituted.
Pure functional project: no nn.Module, no optimizer, no gradients, no caches; models() returns an empty mapping and reset() performs no state restoration.
Tensors live on context['device'] (the worker-bound device), never a hard-coded physical GPU; no default process group is initialized (single-device request, distributed_backend is null).
No downloads, no external assets; the empty assets field is expected because the source explicitly declares the seeded synthetic tensors as the task data.
